relationships: Operator and model steering submit proposals without acquiring execution or activation authority.
Compatibility APIs, automation, and peers feed the same deterministic control plane.
The control plane compiles, admits, executes, evaluates, decides, activates, and observes bounded work.
Measured gaps become typed candidates that are realized, evaluated, rolled out, and decided through one governed improvement cycle.
Durable outcomes drive the next proposal under explicit budgets and stop conditions.
Execution domains use the Go host reference, CUDA runtime, and multimodal compute substrate.
OvergoDB records the identities, lineage, receipts, metrics, decisions, checkpoints, and active state required to reproduce every transition.
Remote peers remain bounded execution adapters and do not own control-plane state.
claim_boundary: The figure describes supervised system-level RSI implemented in the repository.
The figure does not claim unattended operation at scale.
The figure does not claim autonomous improvement of the proposing model's cognition.
A compiled mechanism is not a model-specific compatibility claim without corresponding artifact evidence.
rendering_constraints: Keep the five numbered layers visually distinct and aligned.
Preserve the eight-stage deterministic control plane as the dominant left-to-right sequence.
Keep the governed improvement cycle visually distinct from the execution domains.
Use orthogonal connectors with visible arrowheads.
Terminate every connector exactly at a box, bus, or foundation-band border.
Do not route connectors through component boxes, labels, section titles, or runtime annotations.
Keep control, evidence, and policy paths visually distinct.
Do not imply that model steering or remote peers own control-plane authority.
Do not imply that every execution domain supports every modality.
Keep all labels legible at approximately 1200 pixels display width.
Do not add claims that are not represented in the repository.
Treat this JSON as the editable semantic specification and the PNG as its reviewed rendering.
